question: Does TRL PR #6024's DAPO loss-normalizer correction remove the pre-fix dependence of the mean per-window gradient scale on the ratio between current gradient accumulation and steps per generation?
scope: CPU autograd audit of the exact normalizer expression in two pinned TRL source revisions, using fixed scalar per-token gradient contributions and variable token counts. This does not instantiate GRPOTrainer, update model parameters, or measure task success.

estimand.description: At frozen policy parameters and world_size=1, for each accumulation window w, compute the gradient of the source DAPO masked-token numerator divided by the source normalizer. The primary estimand is the arithmetic mean of per-window gradients divided by the full-generation masked-token-mean gradient.
estimand.N: total valid completion tokens across the generation batch
estimand.control: A=S must leave the source correction at 1; eval mode must leave the normalizer unscaled.

frozen_input.windowing: Consecutive microbatches are accumulated in groups of A; no resampling or token filtering.

secondary_metrics: per-window gradient values for baseline and fixed source expressions
source revision and full-file SHA-256 checks
failure_criteria: either pinned source file hash differs
the fix fails any predeclared gradient-scale criterion
the baseline does not show the predicted A/S scale under this estimand
claim_limits: This is a quantitative source-derived loss/gradient audit, not an end-to-end trainer run.
The fixed per-token contributions are controlled inputs, not model-generated trajectories.
No policy parameter update, convergence, reward quality, or task capability is measured.
The upstream issue and fix are pre-existing; VARE contributes an independent numerical reproduction, not a novel algorithm or new upstream defect.
